abstract: Despite recent advances in camera-based online HD map construction, these systems remain susceptible to sensor failures due to their reliance on onboard cameras. In contrast, satellite images remain available independently of real-time sensing conditions as they are cached offline. Existing methods utilizing satellite images, however, primarily leverage them under nominal conditions, without explicitly addressing them as redundancy when a sensor degrades. To address this gap, we propose ReSMap, a redundancy-aware camera-satellite fusion framework for robust online HD map construction. Our framework explicitly leverages satellite images as a complementary source to improve robustness against camera failures. A Predict-then-Fuse (PTF) module fuses camera and satellite BEV features by using each branch’s own prediction confidence as a per-pixel reliability weight, with no learned router. An Object-Centric Cooperative Multi-modal Query (OCMQ) decoder then extends this per-modality separation to the query level: each modality cross-attends only to its own BEV, and per-modality updates are merged through a learned per-token gate. Our model achieves state-of-the-art performance on nuScenes across all splits and range settings. More importantly, it also sets the new state-of-the-art under camera-failure scenarios, demonstrating that satellite images serve not only as a strong prior but as practical redundancy for robust online HD mapping. Project page: https://dehsurc.github.io/resmap-page/

sections.body: Onboard cameras can become partly or fully unavailable from hardware faults, occlusion, or signal loss, and their evidence grows sparse at longer range. LiDAR remains tied to the onboard sensor stack, and SD maps lack dense lane-level geometry. The paper recasts satellite images as an offline-cached redundancy modality that stays available when sensing degrades. Two designs implement this: Predict-then-Fuse (PTF) fuses camera and satellite BEV features, and the Object-Centric Cooperative Multi-modal Query (OCMQ) decoder keeps per-modality query updates separate before merging them. The authors report the best results across evaluation settings and better performance than external-modality methods under sensor degradation.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Satellite images are proposed as offline redundancy for camera-based online HD map construction when sensors degrade.

sections.body: Existing HD map fusion designs use channel concatenation with residual convolution, learned gated refinement, masked cross-attention, or learned routers. These designs assume all inputs are reliable at inference, so corrupted evidence can pass through residual paths, attention updates, or routing weights. Failure-aware work targets camera-LiDAR or camera-radar failures at the BEV level, and prediction-aware dense fusion weights branches by confidence, but those cues stay inside fusion and do not reach the decoder. Existing decoders fuse modalities before decoding, mix them sequentially, or add parallel cross-attention outputs, so corruption from imperfect fusion still propagates. The paper's approach weights modalities in both fusion and decoding.
sections.heading: Related Work
sections.headline: Prior fusion designs assume all modalities are reliable, so corruption can pass through fusion and the decoder.

sections.body: The model takes multi-view camera images and an ego-centered satellite image and outputs vectorized map instances in the ego BEV frame. Two independent encoders produce camera and satellite BEV features, and each has a BEV segmentation decoder. Predict-then-Fuse uses each branch's maximum class-wise sigmoid confidence as a per-pixel weight, with no learnable fusion weights and stop-gradient on the weights. The OCMQ decoder keeps one object-query set for matching, but each layer computes camera, satellite and fused updates with per-modality deformable cross-attention, then merges them through a learned per-token gate. The merge omits a residual to the previous query so down-weighted modality information cannot re-enter.
sections.heading: Method
sections.headline: Two modules fuse camera and satellite BEV features by prediction confidence and keep modality-specific query updates.

sections.body: Evaluated on the geographically non-overlapping nuScenes split, the temporal model reaches 54.9 mAP at 60 m by 30 m and 47.3 mAP without temporal modeling. These exceed camera-only MapTracker (+14.6 mAP), LiDAR-fused DAMap (+15.5 mAP) and PriorDrive (+12.4 mAP). Under all-camera dropout, the temporal model scores 32.9 mAP against 0.1 for MapTracker. Ablations show that PTF gives the highest clean mIoU (53.5) and the smallest drops, and that gated query merging is best in every column.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: The temporal model scores 54.9 mean average precision clean and 32.9 with all cameras dropped.

sections.body: The paper treats satellite images as both a spatial prior and a redundancy source that stays available when cameras fail. Predict-then-Fuse mixes the two BEV streams with no learnable weights, and the OCMQ decoder recombines per-modality query updates through a learned per-token gate. The authors state the model reaches the best reported performance under clean conditions and under camera failure. The method assumes the satellite image is accurately localized, and GPS or INS errors cause misalignment that Section A.6 quantifies. Cached tiles must also be current, since re-striping or construction weakens the prior. The regime where satellite views carry little usable evidence, such as shadows, tunnels, canopy or tall buildings, is left to future work.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: Localization error, outdated tiles, and occluded top-down views are the stated limits of the satellite fallback.

sections.body: The appendix gives the three-stage training schedule on four RTX 4090 GPUs, the architecture and loss-weight settings, and BEV-feature dropout augmentation. It reports the original nuScenes split, where the model reaches 84.9 mAP with temporal memory and 82.8 without. It also gives Argoverse 2 results with Google Maps tiles, where the temporal model keeps 30.9 mAP under all-camera drop. Further sections cover MapBench corruption metrics, a gate-response analysis of the temporal and non-temporal variants, and additional qualitative comparisons.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix lists training details, original-split and Argoverse 2 results, MapBench robustness metrics, and extra qualitative examples.
